content: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate interacts with various drugs and substances, primarily by affecting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, or other mechanisms. These interactions can lead to increased or decreased drug levels, altered therapeutic effects, or heightened toxicity. Below is a detailed explanation of these interactions: 1. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Prednisolone/Prednisone: Erythromycin increases the levels or effects of prednisolone and prednisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, prednisone decreases erythromycin levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 2. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Pretomanid: Co-administration increases the risk of hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents. Use alternative drugs. 3. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and QTc-Prolonging Drugs (e.g., Primaquine, Prochlorperazine, Promazine, Promethazine, Quetiapine, Quinidine, Sertraline, Sevoflurane, Siponimod, Tacrolimus, Trazodone, Thioridazine, Ziprasidone, etc.): Both agents prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Protamines: Erythromycin increases protamine effects by reducing metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Rifabutin/Rifampin/Rifapentine: Rifabutin levels increase, while erythromycin levels decrease due to CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Ranolazine: Erythromycin increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Venetoclax: Erythromycin increases venetoclax levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Reduce venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor for toxicity. 8. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Verapamil: Both drugs increase each other’s levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, leading to potential toxicity. Contraindicated. 9. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Live Typhoid Vaccine: Erythromycin reduces vaccine efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering the vaccine. 10. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Bedaquiline: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor ECG closely. 11. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Cannabidiol: Erythromycin increases cannabidiol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose. 12. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Atorvastatin: Erythromycin increases atorvastatin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor. 13. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Tadalafil/Avanafil: Erythromycin increases levels of these drugs via CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing the risk of adverse effects. Adjust doses accordingly. 14. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Azithromycin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 15. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Balsalazide: Erythromycin decreases balsalazide levels by altering intestinal flora. Applies only to oral forms. Use caution. 16. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Biotin: Erythromycin decreases biotin levels by altering intestinal flora. Applies only to oral forms. Use caution. 17. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Bortezomib: Erythromycin increases bortezomib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 18. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Calcium Carbonate: Calcium carbonate increases erythromycin levels by an unknown mechanism. Use caution. 19. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Capivasertib: Erythromycin increases capivasertib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce capivasertib dose if co-administered. 20. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Cefdinir/Cefditoren/Cefoxitin/Cefpodoxime: Erythromycin reduces the efficacy of these bactericidal agents through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution. 21. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Bromocriptine: Erythromycin increases bromocriptine levels by an unknown mechanism. Use caution. 22. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Buprenorphine (Subdermal Implant or Long-Acting Injection): Erythromycin increases buprenorphine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for signs of overmedication or toxicity. Adjust therapy as needed. 23. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Cabazitaxel/Cabozantinib: Erythromycin increases levels of these drugs via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 24. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Albuterol/Arformoterol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 25. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Atogepant: Erythromycin increases atogepant levels via OATP1B1 inhibition. Adjust atogepant dose to 10 mg or 30 mg daily. 26. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Bosutinib: Bosutinib increases erythromycin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 27. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Brexpiprazole: Erythromycin increases brexpiprazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Vilazodone: Erythromycin increases vilazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily if adverse effects occur. 29. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Voriconazole: Voriconazole increases erythromycin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Contraindicated. 30. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Zavegepant: Erythromycin increases zavegepant levels via OATP1B3 inhibition. Avoid co-administration. 31. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Bromocriptine: Erythromycin increases bromocriptine levels by an unknown mechanism. Use caution. 32. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Amifampridine: Erythromycin increases seizure risk when co-administered with amifampridine. Monitor closely. 33. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Aluminum Hydroxide: Aluminum hydroxide increases erythromycin levels by an unknown mechanism. Use caution. 34. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Amikacin: Erythromycin increases amikacin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution. 35. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Amiodarone: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Amoxicillin: Erythromycin may reduce the efficacy of amoxicillin by altering intestinal flora. Use caution. 37. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Amlodipine: Erythromycin increases amlodipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 38. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Apomorphine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 39. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Armodafinil: Erythromycin increases armodafinil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 40. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Atazanavir: Erythromycin increases atazanavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 41. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Azithromycin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 42. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Bendamustine: Erythromycin decreases bendamustine efficacy by reducing its conversion to active metabolites. Use caution. 43. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Betrixaban: Erythromycin increases betrixaban levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Reduce betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, then 40 mg daily. 44. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Bexarotene: Erythromycin increases bexarotene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 45. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Bosentan: Erythromycin increases bosentan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 46. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Bromocriptine: Erythromycin increases bromocriptine levels by an unknown mechanism. Use caution. 47. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Budesonide: Erythromycin increases budesonide levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 48. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Buprenorphine: Erythromycin increases buprenorphine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for signs of overmedication or toxicity. 49. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Cabazitaxel: Erythromycin increases cabazitaxel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 50. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Cabozantinib: Erythromycin increases cabozantinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 51. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Calcium Carbonate: Calcium carbonate increases erythromycin levels by an unknown mechanism. Use caution. 52. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Cannabidiol: Erythromycin increases cannabidiol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose. 53. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Capivasertib: Erythromycin increases capivasertib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce capivasertib dose if co-administered. 54. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Cefdinir: Erythromycin reduces cefdinir efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution. 55. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Cefditoren: Erythromycin reduces cefditoren efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution. 56. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Cefoxitin: Erythromycin reduces cefoxitin efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution. 57. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and Cefpodoxime: Erythromycin reduces cefpodoxime efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when erythromycin ethylsuccinate is co-administered with other drugs.
